name: Return lapsed rows to the queue
description:
A lapsed lease returns its row to the queue; the third lapse fails it as LEASE_LAPSED rather than passing it round the fleet for ever.

IT IS A CLOCK, NOT A STEP OF EVERY CLAIM: at N runners polling four lanes that would be 0.8N reaps a second, each scanning an index whose size is itself proportional to N -- quadratic work for a statement that normally matches nothing. Once a second in one place is the same guarantee for a constant cost.

Running it in Soma's Orion is what makes 'one place' true: that node is in CLUSTER mode, so a cron singleton is singular across the whole state database. This is the exact opposite of the rule for a Kalam replica, which must never share cluster state precisely so that its match channels are not singletons.

It stays a separate statement rather than a CTE inside the claim because a CTE's writes are invisible to the claim in the same snapshot, so a row reaped that way would wait one more poll before anyone could take it.

tasks.name: Read the generation and this poller's marker
tasks.description: One MGET, soft: `gen:work` moves with every claim, release, requeue and pairing, and `idle:reap` holds the generation under which the last reap found nothing in flight. Equal means no row has been claimed since, so no lease can have lapsed: the tick is skipped with no statement. A Redis that cannot answer runs the reap.

tasks.name: Skip the tick while nothing is in flight
tasks.description: A skipped tick delays nothing: a lease can only lapse on a row that was claimed, and a claim bumps the generation. The marker's 60 s TTL is the backstop, so the reap runs at least once a minute whatever Redis says.
Rows moved: the match namespace, `gen:work` (a requeued row is new work) and `gen:finished` (a row failed on its third lapse is a verdict to count).

tasks.name: Remember that nothing was in flight
tasks.description: Written only when the reap moved nothing and nothing at all is claimed or running, under the generation read at the top (zero when none exists yet): the next ticks skip until a claim bumps the generation or 60 s pass.
